# FAQ-018: Engineering FAQ #18
Revision: Rev A

Q: What is the required shot media top-up interval for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03), and why is it maintained at that interval?
A: The shot media top-up interval for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 48 hours. Rationale: consistent media level maintains blast energy and part coverage to avoid under- or over-blasting of forgings processed for heat treat preparation. Operational practice: after each shift handover, the operator verifies the media level and records the check in the shot blast log. Example record entries should include equipment id (EQ-P3-L4-SB03), date/time, operator initials, and confirmation that the top-up interval requirement (48 hours) is met or the amount of media added. When topping up, use the approved media grade and follow PPE and containment guidance. Traceability: log entries support quality audits and should be retained per plant record retention policy and referenced when implementing changes under ECN-2026-011.

Q: Which lubricant part number is specified for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02), and what are the service expectations?
A: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is CFW-LUB-195. Rationale: CFW-LUB-195 has been validated for the pressure, temperature stability, and compatibility with seals used on EQ-P1-L4-HP02. Service expectations: use only CFW-LUB-195 for refill and top-off operations on EQ-P1-L4-HP02. Records to keep: maintenance action sheet should identify the equipment id (EQ-P1-L4-HP02), lubricant part number used (CFW-LUB-195), quantity dispensed, date, and technician performing the work. These records provide evidence for lubrication audits and are referenced during change control reviews in ECN-2026-011 and maintenance planning per MM-P1-L2-HT03.

Q: What is the austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02), and what controls are recommended around that setpoint?
A: The austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C. Rationale: the setpoint 845 °C provides the required phase transformation for the machining alloy families processed in that furnace while meeting metallurgical specifications. Controls: verify setpoint programming before each heat cycle and confirm with chart recorder or furnace control display. Records to keep: austenitizing setpoint confirmation should be logged with equipment id (EQ-P2-L3-HT02), setpoint value (845 °C), operator initials, and any deviations or corrective actions. Use these logs to support process capability checks and reference them when aligning procedures with MM-P1-L2-HT03 and during any engineering change reviews under ECN-2026-011.

Q: What is the austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03), and how should variability be documented?
A: The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 855 °C. Rationale: 855 °C is selected to meet the metallurgical profile required for ring rolling lots processed from that heat treat line. Documenting variability: any change from the setpoint 855 °C must be recorded immediately, with justification, approval routing, and associated lot numbers. Records to keep: include equipment id (EQ-P1-L2-HT03), setpoint value (855 °C), lot identifiers, operator, and approver for any deviation. Cross-reference this documentation with MM-P1-L2-HT03 for heat treat control practices and with ECN-2026-011 for formal engineering changes.

Q: What lubricant part number is specified for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03), and what are the handling and record requirements?
A: The lubricant part number for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is CFW-LUB-188. Handling: use only CFW-LUB-188 for components and bearings specified in the IH03 lubrication schedule. Store CFW-LUB-188 in original containers, follow shelf guidance on the container, and apply using calibrated dispensing tools. Records to keep: maintenance log entries must record equipment id (EQ-P1-L1-IH03), lubricant part number applied (CFW-LUB-188), batch or lot number of the lubricant, quantity, date, and technician. These records are required for traceability, troubleshooting, and supplier change verification under SB-1037 and should be produced during internal audits or supplier assessments.

Related documents:
- ECN-2026-011
- MM-P1-L2-HT03
- SB-1037
